sentences.text: El pueblo, antaño bullicioso, languidecía ahora bajo un silencio casi sepulcral.
sentences.translation: The village, once bustling, now languished under an almost sepulchral silence.

sentences.text: Las casas, con las contraventanas cerradas, parecían párpados rendidos al sueño.
sentences.translation: The houses, with their shutters closed, seemed like eyelids surrendered to sleep.

sentences.text: Quienes se quedaron lo hicieron menos por esperanza que por arraigo.
sentences.translation: Those who stayed did so less out of hope than out of attachment.

sentences.text: Don Aurelio, el último maestro, recorría las calles desiertas con paso cansino.
sentences.translation: Don Aurelio, the last schoolmaster, wandered the deserted streets with a weary gait.

sentences.text: Recordaba, no sin cierta congoja, las aulas rebosantes de niños.
sentences.translation: He remembered, not without a certain anguish, the classrooms brimming with children.

sentences.text: El progreso, esa palabra tantas veces invocada, había pasado de largo.
sentences.translation: Progress, that word so often invoked, had passed it by.

sentences.text: Y sin embargo, en cada amanecer persistía un tenue rescoldo de dignidad.
sentences.translation: And yet, in every dawn a faint ember of dignity persisted.

sentences.text: Acaso, pensaba el maestro, la memoria fuera la última forma de resistencia.
sentences.translation: Perhaps, the schoolmaster thought, memory was the last form of resistance.

sentences.text: Mientras hubiera quien recordara, el pueblo no estaría del todo muerto.
sentences.translation: As long as there was someone to remember, the village would not be entirely dead.

questions.question: How is the village described at the start?
What does the schoolmaster see as the last form of resistance?

sentences.text: A lo largo de los años, había recorrido tierras cuyos nombres apenas recuerdo.
sentences.translation: Over the years, I had travelled lands whose names I scarcely remember.

sentences.text: Cada viaje me despojaba de alguna certeza y me regalaba una pregunta nueva.
sentences.translation: Each journey stripped me of some certainty and gave me a new question.

sentences.text: Aprendí que el extranjero no es un lugar, sino una mirada.
sentences.translation: I learned that the foreign is not a place, but a way of looking.

sentences.text: En los mercados de Oriente, el bullicio se entreveraba con aromas indescriptibles.
sentences.translation: In the markets of the East, the hubbub intermingled with indescribable aromas.

sentences.text: Hubo noches en que la soledad pesaba más que cualquier equipaje.
sentences.translation: There were nights when loneliness weighed more than any luggage.

sentences.text: No obstante, jamás me arrepentí de haber partido.
sentences.translation: Nevertheless, I never regretted having left.

sentences.text: Quien no se atreve a perderse difícilmente llega a encontrarse.
sentences.translation: Whoever does not dare to get lost can hardly come to find themselves.

sentences.text: Hoy, ya anciano, comprendo que el verdadero destino era el propio camino.
sentences.translation: Today, now an old man, I understand that the true destination was the journey itself.

sentences.text: Y si pudiera, lo recorrería de nuevo sin cambiar una sola encrucijada.
sentences.translation: And if I could, I would travel it again without changing a single crossroads.

questions.question: What did each journey give the narrator?
How does the narrator define 'the foreign'?
What does he conclude the true destination was?
